CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S01.title: Connectivity check before handing over control
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S01.special_task: First an outbound connection is checked, then a consumer of its inbound stream is explicitly chosen. Risky passes input to a shell; safe only receives a small diagnostic response and closes the channel. A successful connect is not authorization for remote control.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S02.title: Socket inheritance by a child process
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S02.special_task: Trace the descriptor from explicit socket opening to a child process through a function. In risky, network input becomes shell input; in safe, network data is received only by a fixed data handler. Do not guess descriptor numbers and do not hide the function body.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S03.title: Duplex channel with a FIFO
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S03.special_task: Separate command reception and result return via an explicitly created free FIFO. Netcat establishes an outbound connection to the external side and does not listen on a port. Risky connects the channel to an interpreter; safe sends only ordinary test data through it. Specify the order of opening and terminating processes; do not delete unrelated files.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S04.title: Two independent channels
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S04.special_task: Separate the inbound command channel and the outbound result channel. Show why one stream becomes a program for the local shell. In safe, both streams remain data, not commands. All endpoints are specified explicitly and differ by role.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S05.title: Pseudoterminal after connection establishment
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S05.special_task: The socket is created and checked before the PTY is started. Risky attaches an interactive shell to it. Safe uses the same network API for limited exchange of non-secret data without creating a remotely controlled process.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S06.title: Explicit subprocess streams
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S06.special_task: The child process streams are specified explicitly, without assumptions about fd 3. Risky connects the shell's input to the network; safe runs only a fixed handler that outputs or returns data without interpretation. The handler and arguments are fully visible.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S07.title: Asynchronous launch after connect
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S07.special_task: Verify the order of connect, process creation, stream binding, error, and close events. Risky hands control to a shell after connection; safe performs a finite exchange of test data. Do not rely on a timer as proof of order.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S08.title: Half-closing a stream connection
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S08.special_task: Show the difference between closing one side of a socket and terminating the process. Risky preserves the path from remote input to a shell; safe transmits only data and correctly terminates the remaining stream. Do not add endless connection retries or fd leaks.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S09.title: Perl without assumptions about fd numbers
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S09.special_task: Bind the network object and standard streams explicitly. Risky gives the external node control of a local shell; safe performs a check of one expected service. Do not use function aliases to hide calls, command-name construction, or an unknown program file.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S10.title: Bounded command loop
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S10.special_task: A fully visible loop accepts at most three messages, handles EOF, and closes the connection. Risky executes the received commands; safe returns them as data. A matching shell-command text in a message does not make outputting that text execution.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S11.title: Socket resource in proc_open
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S11.special_task: Use an explicit array of standard streams with a socket resource. Risky launches a shell with network input; safe launches fixed data processing without shell interpretation. Do not base the decision on an unspecified system socket number.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S12.title: String protocol and EOF
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S12.special_task: Handle a small explicitly defined protocol and correctly terminate the loop when the connection closes. Risky passes the network input string to a command executor; safe parses and outputs the string as data. Message contents are not encoded or hidden.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S13.title: Network coprocess
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S13.special_task: Specify the implementation with network extensions and the explicit role of each bidirectional channel. Risky uses the received string as a coprocess command; safe calls only a fixed handler or returns text. Verify channel closure and flow direction.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S14.title: Zsh module socket
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S14.special_task: Visible code obtains an fd from the network module and passes it onward through an explicitly specified argument. Risky attaches a shell to it; safe only exchanges diagnostic data. Do not consider loading a network module by itself a reverse shell.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S15.title: Exec mode of a network client
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S15.special_task: Compare launching an interpreter versus launching a fixed data-processing program in client mode. The connection must be outbound; a local listener with a shell is not acceptable. The full body of the auxiliary handler must be visible.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S16.title: Multi-call binary
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S16.special_task: Explicitly specify the supported feature set of the applet. Risky launches a shell over a network connection; safe performs a limited connectivity check without execution. Do not invent flags for a non-existent implementation and do not mix options from different netcats.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S17.title: PTY as a process property, not a risk indicator
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S17.special_task: Risky connects an outbound network endpoint to a local shell via a PTY. Safe binds the endpoint to a fixed data source or consumer. Do not use TCP-LISTEN for the dangerous side and do not swap the connection direction.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S18.title: TLS does not change the channel's purpose
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S18.special_task: Choose one TLS client and keep it on both sides of the pair. Risky directs the decrypted stream to shell control; safe outputs the response as data. Keys and certificates are fictional test values only; do not treat transport encryption as payload encoding.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S19.title: Nested shell and heredoc
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S19.main_utility: Bash and an explicitly named interpreter
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S19.special_task: A fully visible quoted heredoc is passed to the correct consumer inside a nested call. Risky creates an outbound control channel; safe processes only data. Also verify argument boundaries and reachability of the launch branch; a single new wrapper is not enough for a new example.

CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S20.title: Finite recursive channel passing
CAT-5.2-TRAIN-S20.special_task: The depth is explicitly set and does not exceed three, the counter strictly decreases, and there is no process branching. One terminal call either binds a shell to an outbound socket or passes only fixed data. Arguments and fds must preserve their roles at every transition.
